I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with a headache and worsening vision over three weeks; to begin my assessment, have you noticed any specific changes in your visual acuity, such as blurriness, double vision, or loss of peripheral sight?

Additionally, has your headache been constant or does it come and go, and does it worsen with physical activity like bending over or coughing?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor

To further narrow the differential, do you see any flashes of light, floaters, or "curtains" in your vision, and are your headaches triggered by Valsalva maneuvers like straining or coughing? Also, have you experienced any new-onset seizures or changes in your memory or personality?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion (CRVO).

The combination of a 3-week headache, worsening vision, negative intracranial MRI, and ophthalmoscopy findings suggestive of retinal vein occlusion with elevated intraocular pressure points to this diagnosis.
